title: 1st Truth The Testimony Of Createdness In The Cosmos

questions.question: What impossible idea is rejected before the passage concludes that a Necessary Existent must exist?
questions.answer: It rejects the idea that things can bring each other into being through an endless chain of causes.

questions.question: After that false idea is rejected, what is said must exist?
questions.answer: A being whose existence is necessary and unlike anything else must exist.

questions.question: How are all other beings described in relation to that Necessary Existent?
questions.answer: They are described as dependent and brought into existence by Him.

questions.question: What major truth is said to fill the whole universe?
questions.answer: The truth that created things come into existence and do not exist on their own is found throughout the universe.

questions.question: Which season is used as a clear example of widespread death in the world?
questions.answer: Autumn.

questions.question: What kinds of living things are especially mentioned as dying in huge numbers in that season?
questions.answer: Many kinds of plants and small animals.

questions.question: How is each member of those species described to show its value and complexity?
questions.answer: Each one is presented as being like a small world by itself.

questions.question: Is that dying shown as random chaos or as something arranged with wisdom? Explain.
questions.answer: It is shown as highly ordered and controlled, not random.

questions.question: What do living things leave behind after they die?
questions.answer: They leave seeds and eggs behind.

questions.question: What future purpose do those seeds and eggs serve?
questions.answer: They become the means for new life and return in the spring.

questions.question: What do the seeds and eggs suggest about mercy, wisdom, power, and knowledge?
questions.answer: They show signs of all four by preserving life in a planned and caring way.

questions.question: What is meant by saying the dying creatures pass on their “record” and “program” before they die?
questions.answer: It means the information for their future life and growth is preserved in what they leave behind.

questions.question: To whom are those seeds and eggs entrusted?
questions.answer: They are entrusted to the protection and wisdom of the Divine Preserver.

questions.question: What main conclusion does this whole example support?
questions.answer: It supports that creation is real, life is controlled by Allah, and beings do not exist by themselves.

questions.question: Why does the passage say things cannot be the makers of one another?
questions.answer: Because that would lead to an unreasonable system where causes keep depending on earlier causes without end.

questions.question: What word best describes the being whose existence cannot be avoided according to the passage?
questions.answer: Necessary.

questions.question: What does the passage say about anything equal or similar to that being?
questions.answer: It says no true equal or match to Him can exist.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the status of everything besides Him?
questions.answer: Everything else is possible in existence, not necessary, and is created by Him.

questions.question: Which part of nature gives a visible lesson about createdness right in front of us?
questions.answer: The dying of life in autumn.

questions.question: About how broad is that autumn dying described to be?
questions.answer: It is described as the death of a whole world of living things.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention many different species instead of just one?
questions.answer: To show that this pattern is widespread and not limited to a single kind of life.

questions.question: What idea is supported by the statement that each creature is like a tiny cosmos?
questions.answer: It shows that even small beings are complex and carefully made.

questions.question: What shows that death in nature is not the end of the story?
questions.answer: Seeds and eggs remain behind for life to return later.

questions.question: In what season is revival expected to happen?
questions.answer: In spring.

questions.question: What can a reader infer from the survival of seeds and eggs after the death of the larger living things?
questions.answer: Life is preserved according to a plan, even when the visible creature dies.

questions.question: Why are the return of life and the preservation of its pattern called signs of mercy and wisdom?
questions.answer: Because they show care, purpose, and exact planning rather than waste or confusion.

questions.question: What does it mean that the creatures hand over their life-pattern before dying?
questions.answer: It means their future form and function are stored in what remains from them.

questions.question: What overall belief about Allah does this passage strengthen?
questions.answer: It strengthens belief that Allah alone creates, preserves, and brings life back in an ordered way.

questions.question: What false explanation of existence is ruled out at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: The explanation that beings produce each other through endless causation is ruled out.

questions.question: Once that explanation is ruled out, what kind of being must be accepted?
questions.answer: A unique being whose existence is necessary must be accepted.

questions.question: What two qualities are given to everything other than that being?
questions.answer: They are possible in existence and created.

questions.question: Does the passage present createdness as a small idea or as something spread through all creation?
questions.answer: It presents it as spread through all creation.

questions.question: Which examples can people directly observe with their eyes?
questions.answer: They can directly observe the widespread dying of living things in autumn.

questions.question: Why is autumn an effective example for the argument?
questions.answer: Because it shows large-scale ending of life happening again and again in front of people.

questions.question: What balances the sadness of death in the passage’s description of autumn?
questions.answer: The promise of future life through seeds and eggs balances it.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the manner in which living things die?
questions.answer: They die in a disciplined and organized way.

questions.question: What important job do seeds and eggs carry after death happens?
questions.answer: They preserve what is needed for life to begin again.

questions.question: What do the preserved traces of life show about divine knowledge?
questions.answer: They show that every creature’s form and life-plan are known and guarded.

questions.question: Why is the Preserver mentioned in connection with seeds and eggs?
questions.answer: To show that their safekeeping and future growth depend on Allah’s protection.

questions.question: What connection does the passage make between death and rebirth?
questions.answer: Death is shown as part of a cycle that prepares the way for renewed life.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly trying to help the reader understand through these natural scenes?
questions.answer: It is helping the reader see that the universe points to Allah as the Creator and Keeper of life.

questions.question: According to the passage, what makes an endless chain of causes unacceptable?
questions.answer: It is unacceptable because it leads to an absurd explanation that never truly accounts for existence.

questions.question: Instead of endless dependence between created things, what final reality is affirmed?
questions.answer: A Necessary Existent is affirmed as the true source.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the possibility of another being exactly like Him?
questions.answer: It says that such a match is impossible.

questions.question: What relationship do all created things have to Him?
questions.answer: They depend on Him for their existence.

questions.question: What truth is said to be visible throughout the universe?
questions.answer: The truth that things are created and do not last on their own.

questions.question: What yearly event helps show that living things are not self-sustaining?
questions.answer: The mass dying that comes in autumn.

questions.question: Why does the passage include both plants and small animals in its example?
questions.answer: It shows that the pattern reaches across different forms of life.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the death of these living things: careless or measured?
questions.answer: It describes their death as measured and orderly.

questions.question: What remains in place after these living things die?
questions.answer: Seeds and eggs remain behind.

questions.question: What do those remains make possible later on?
questions.answer: They make new life and renewed existence possible in spring.

questions.question: What can students infer from the idea that these remains contain a life-plan?
questions.answer: They can infer that life is designed with purpose and stored information, not left to blind chance.

questions.question: Why are those remains connected with divine protection?
questions.answer: Because their future role depends on Allah’s guarding and preserving them.

questions.question: What lesson about Allah’s attributes comes from the careful transfer from dying life to future life?
questions.answer: It points to His mercy, wisdom, power, and knowledge.

questions.question: State the main argument of the whole passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: The changing life of the world shows that created things cannot create themselves, so all creation points to Allah, the only Necessary Existent.

questions.question: What does the passage say is impossible for created things to do to one another?
questions.answer: It says they cannot be the ultimate creators of one another.

questions.question: What problem comes from saying one created thing causes another forever with no end?
questions.answer: That idea never reaches a true first source, so it fails as an explanation.

questions.question: Who is the only true source of existence according to the passage?
questions.answer: The Necessary Existent, who has no equal.

questions.question: How are the rest of beings classified?
questions.answer: They are dependent and created beings.

questions.question: Where does the passage say we can easily notice the mark of createdness?
questions.answer: We can notice it in the visible world around us.

questions.question: What season pictures this truth in a powerful way?
questions.answer: Autumn.

questions.question: What happens in autumn that makes the argument strong?
questions.answer: Vast numbers of living things pass away.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare one small creature to a whole world?
questions.answer: To show how much detail and order are found even in a single life.

questions.question: What prevents the scene of autumn from being only a story of loss?
questions.answer: The creatures leave behind seeds and eggs that carry the future.

questions.question: What does spring represent in the passage?
questions.answer: It represents return, renewal, and life after apparent ending.

questions.question: What kind of “miracles” are seen in the return of life through seeds and eggs?
questions.answer: They are signs of compassion, wisdom, power, and knowledge.

questions.question: What is being protected when seeds and eggs are preserved?
questions.answer: The pattern, future growth, and life-history of the creatures are being protected.

questions.question: What does the title “Glorious Preserver” help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader understand that Allah keeps and guards creation with honor and care.

questions.question: How does the passage move from observing nature to believing in Allah?
questions.answer: It uses repeated patterns of death and return in nature as evidence that Allah alone creates, preserves, and brings life back.

questions.question: What wrong idea about causes is dismissed at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: The idea that creation can be explained by things causing one another endlessly is dismissed.

questions.question: What necessary conclusion follows from dismissing that idea?
questions.answer: There must be one being whose existence does not depend on anything else.

questions.question: What does the passage say about any rival to that being?
questions.answer: No rival or true likeness to Him is possible.

questions.question: What do we learn about everything besides Him?
questions.answer: Everything besides Him is brought into existence and is not necessary by itself.

questions.question: What large truth is said to spread through the universe?
questions.answer: The truth that the world and its beings are created.

questions.question: Which part of that truth can people see directly?
questions.answer: They can directly see widespread death among living things.

questions.question: In which season does this visible example appear most clearly?
questions.answer: In autumn.

questions.question: What detail shows that the passage is speaking about many forms of life, not just a few?
questions.answer: It mentions huge numbers of different species of plants and small animals.

questions.question: How is their death described in terms of order?
questions.answer: Their death happens in a controlled and purposeful pattern.

questions.question: What do they leave as a trust for the future?
questions.answer: They leave seeds and eggs.

questions.question: Why are those seeds and eggs so important in the argument?
questions.answer: They show that life continues according to a preserved design after the visible creature dies.

questions.question: What does the image of handing over a “record” suggest about living things?
questions.answer: It suggests that their actions, pattern, and future form are kept محفوظly in what they leave behind.

questions.question: What role does Allah’s protection play in this process?
questions.answer: Allah guards what is left behind so it can serve as the starting point for renewed life.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the passage’s message?
questions.answer: The ordered cycle of death and renewal in nature proves that created beings are under Allah’s control and depend on Him, the one Necessary Existent.
